ExpeditionsinAnatolia
One of the most important accomplishments of
Hazrat Muawiyawasthebuilding ofastrong navyto
weakenthestrengthoftheByzantine Empirein
the eastern Mediterranean. A navy was built
which captured Rhodes and other islands in the
eastern Mediterranean in671AD.
In 674 AD, Constantinople, the capital of the
Byzantine Empire, was besieged. The Muslim
armies continued this besiege from 674 to 678
AD but were later forced back to eastern
Anatolia. One of the most famous martyrs of
this war was Hazrat Abu Ayyub Al Ansari who
was stll out in the path of Allah at the age of 80.

On eastern front, armies were sent to Khurasan and Sindh by Hazrat Mu'awiya . Later,
underSultanAbdul Malik(685-705AD),theMuslimarmies invadedMakranandSindhin
the Subcontinent. In Central.Asia they conquered Bukhara, Samarkand, Khwarazm,
Fergana,and Tashkant.Many of these conquests came in the time of great Muslim general
Qutayba Bin Muslim who was also governor of Khurasan during the reign of Walid Bin
AbdulMalik(705ADto715AD).
Another important conquestduring thetimeof Caliph Walidwasof Sindh.Muhammad
Bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD. This marked the beginning of Muslim
presence in the Subcontinent.
